severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Sections 8.2, 8.3 and 10.4; Table 7 Olsen Grade of Actinic Keratoses: "8.2 Inclusion Criteria" "© contains >4 to <12 clinically typical, visible, and discrete (non-confluent) AK lesions" "a) Clinically atypical and/or rapidly changing AK lesions in the TF" "b) Hyperkeratotic or hypertrophic lesions, recalcitrant disease (defined as failure to respond" "At Baseline/Day 1, the dermatologist will classify each visible, discrete, non-hypertrophic," "non-hyperkeratotic AK lesion as Olsen 1 or 2, as per Table 7." "Patients with Olsen Grade 3" "lesions in the TF are excluded fiom the study, as these are considered" "hyperkeratotic/hypertrophic for the purposes of this study (see Section 8.3)." "Table 7 Olsen Grade of Actinic Keratoses" "ee eee Slight palpability, with actinic keratoses felt better than seen" "Moderately thick actinic keratoses that are easily seen and felt" "Very thick and/or obvious actinic keratoses" -- The protocol identifies Olsen grades 1 and 2 for baseline lesions and excludes grade 3; grade 3 is described as hyperkeratotic/hypertrophic. The schedule names Baseline/Day 1, not a numbered baseline visit, so baseline_visit_number is null. The separate lesion-count eligibility criterion is not represented because the closed ScoreCriterion metrics do not encode lesion counts. Severity is graded but not literally labeled moderate-to-severe.

prohibited_concomitant: Core Study: any non-study drug on the treatment field is prohibited, except when the Investigator considers topical treatment necessary for safety (for example, a corticosteroid).
permitted_concomitant: For safety reasons, topical treatment (for example, a corticosteroid) may be applied to the treatment field if the Investigator considers it necessary; the patient should be encouraged to continue study assessments.
Physical treatments for actinic keratosis are permitted only for lesions more than 2 cm outside the treatment field.
Therapies not restricted by the protocol may be used.
value.population_note: The treatment-field restriction and its safety exception apply during the Core Study. The cited protocol does not establish a standardized background regimen or an overall monotherapy classification.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 9.9.2.1 Core Study, concomitant medications and therapies: "The use of physical treatments for AK (eg, cryotherapy) is permitted only for lesions >2 cm" "outside of the TF." "The use of any non-study drug on the TF is prohibited during the study." "If for safety reasons" "the Investigator considers it necessary to apply topical treatment (eg, corticosteroid) to the TF" "during the study, then the patient should be encouraged to continue in the study in order to" "allow further assessments." "Therapies (medication and non-medication therapies) not restricted by the protocol may be" "used." -- Preserves the treatment-field prohibition's express safety exception and its Core Study scope; records the separate outside-field physical-treatment allowance and the general allowance for therapies not restricted by protocol.

value.dosing_interval: Once daily for 5 consecutive days per course; a second core-study course starts 8 weeks after the first course, and follow-up courses are at least 16 weeks after the most recent course.

primary_endpoint_refs.label: Percent change from baseline in lesion count at Day 57

value.source_inconsistency: The protocol's schedule and duration describe follow-up through Week 48 (with a final visit or telephone contact then), but section 8.8.1 defines end of trial as the last visit at Day 113 or earlier. Both statements are from the same protocol; the discrepancy is preserved rather than harmonized.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Protocol Synopsis Trial Duration; Trial Design; Tables 1 and 2 Schedule of Assessments; 8.8.1 End of Trial Definition; 11.10.1 Primary Endpoint: "The study is comprised of a 4-week Screening Period, a 16-week double-blind Treatment and" "Response Assessment Period (core study), and a 32-week Follow-Up Period." "The study is comprised of a 4-week Screening Period, a 16-week double-blind Treatment and" "Response Assessment Period (core study), and a 32-week Follow-Up Period." "(tirbanibulin 10 mg/g ointment or placebo [vehicle]) once daily for 5 days beginning on Day 1." "All patients will be evaluated for efficacy, safety, and tolerability at Days 8, 15, 29, and 57." "Those patients who do not achieve CC at Day 57 will receive a second 5-day course of the" "randomised treatment." "Patients receiving a second treatment course will also be evaluated for" "efficacy, safety, and tolerability at Days 64, 71, and 85." "receive one or two treatment courses, will be evaluated at Day 113 (Week 16)." "Patients who achieve CC (no lesions in the treatment field at either Day 57 or Day 113) will" "have the opportunity to receive treatment courses with tirbanibulin 10 mg/g ointment, as" "needed, during the Follow-up Period." "lesions in the treatment field at FUP1 will receive a course of tirbanibulin 10 mg/g ointment, if" "at least 16 weeks have elapsed since starting the most recent treatment course (ie, patients who" "Follow-Up Period visit 2 (FUP2) will occur 16 weeks after FUP1." "with lesions in the treatment field at FUP2 will receive a course of tirbanibulin 10 mg/g" "Patients who do not achieve CC at either Day 57 or Day 113 will not be treated with study drug" "No site visits are required, and safety data collection will be done remotely (ie," "by telephone or other means) (Table 2)." "All patients will have a final visit or telephone contact at Week 48." "The duration of each treatment course is 5 days." "The total duration of each patient’s participation in the study is approximately 12 months," "including the 4-week Screening Period, a 16-week double-blind Treatment and Response" "Assessment Period, and a 32-week Follow-Up Period." "Table 1: Schedule of Assessments — Screening Period and Treatment and Response Assessment Period" "(Baseline) (Week 8) (Week 16)" "Table 2: Schedule of Assessments — Follow-Up Period" "(Week 16) (Week 32) (Week 48)" "is defined as the date of the last visit of the last patient, either at Day 113 or" "earlier, if the last patient discontinues prematurely." "The primary endpoint, the percent change from baseline in lesion count at Day 57 (Week 8)," "Day(s) -28 to -1 1 245 29 57 71 113" "Day(s) 113 +4 days 225 +4 days 337" "Day(s) 113 +4 days 225 +4 days 337" -- Protocol version 3.0 dated 31 January 2024 is used. Table 1 provides the full visit schedule; Table 2 provides follow-up visits. Day 64, 71, and 85 assessments apply only after a second treatment course; follow-up assessments depend on clearance status, and patients without complete clearance have remote safety follow-up. Screening is Day -28 to -1; screening_days=28 is the exact conversion of the stated four weeks (4 x 7 days). The screening period start_week=-4 is relative to Day 1, using the stated Day -28 screening start; Day 1 is week 0. Total duration 52 weeks is approximate arithmetic: four weeks of screening plus the stated final Week 48 from Day 1. Table 2 explicitly gives Days 225 and 337 at Weeks 32 and 48. The nominal FUP2/3 schedule is Week 32/48, spaced 16 weeks after FUP1; periods and key outcome timing are reported relative to Day 1. The protocol schedule table makes full visit-table availability true.
